speaker: seraphina
text: Hi! Let's play!
note: The title screen greeting — the first thing the game ever says. Spoken with a comma: edge-tts puts a full second of silence after a mid-line '!', which on screen is a second with no word lit. The comma keeps the beat without the dead air.

speaker: seraphina
text: I need your help making sure Dad never finds this!

speaker: seraphina
text: Sss — Sparky!
note: edge-tts reads any run of s's as the letter NAME, repeated: 'Sss' comes out 'ess ess ess'. 'Suh' at least leads with a real /s/. Placeholder until ElevenLabs — see the voice_pipeline_spike report.

speaker: seraphina
text: Mmm — Munchy wants the mango.

speaker: seraphina
text: Ooh, did something sparkle?
note: The well. Hers, not Dad's: nobody is standing at the well, so what she hears is herself wondering. See the narrative-voice rule in CLAUDE.md.

speaker: dad
text: Time for bed!
note: Called from inside the house when the light starts going, once a day and never again — see the day clock. He is not a person standing in the world and there is no plan for him to be one, so the balloon is anchored at the front door instead: the words come out of the house. The one line in the game not spoken by somebody on screen, and the one exception to the narrative-voice rule in CLAUDE.md — this is Dad talking, not the world.

speaker: seraphina
text: I want to pick an apple!

speaker: seraphina
text: I want to read a book!

speaker: seraphina
text: Again! Again!
note: Spoken with a comma: edge-tts leaves a full second of silence after a mid-line '!', which on screen is a second with no word lit. Same trick as seraphina_hello.

speaker: seraphina
text: Wardrobe

speaker: seraphina
text: My cozy bed. Time to sleep!
note: The bed is the sleep trigger now, so its line is the offer as well as the name: press green once and she says this, press it again while it is still in the air and the day ends. Two sentences on purpose — the first is still the word the prop is teaching, the second is the question. Hers, not Dad's: dad_bedtime is kept below for the day Dad is a person standing in the room.

speaker: sneak
text: My spell book says faeries are REAL. I'm going to prove it!
say: My spell book says faeries are real. I'm going to prove it!
note: Shown in capitals and spoken as a word: edge-tts reads a short run of capitals as letters, and 'R E A L' is not what he means. The say/text split keeps the emphasis on screen without spelling it aloud.

speaker: sneak
text: Shhh! This book is full of secrets.
say: Shhh, this book is full of secrets.
note: Comma, not a bang: edge-tts puts a full second of silence after a mid-line '!', which on screen is a second with no word lit. Same fix as seraphina_hello.

speaker: hazel
text: Hi Seraphina! Wanna play?
note: The mid-line '!' silence again.

speaker: hazel
text: I found a shiny pebble!

speaker: sneak
text: My spell book has a faerie spell! We need three magic stones.
say: My spell book has a faerie spell. We need three magic stones.
note: The faerie quest, offered. Full stop where the text has a bang: edge-tts puts a full second of silence after a mid-line '!', which on screen is a second with no word lit.

speaker: sneak
text: A ruby, a sapphire, and a malachite! You'll need a hammer to crack them.
say: A ruby, a sapphire, and a malachite. You'll need a hammer to crack them.
note: The second half of the offer. Same mid-line '!' fix.

speaker: sneak
text: I saw a hammer near the well!
note: Phase one's instruction, and what the yellow button replays. The bang is line-final, so it costs nothing and no say split is needed.

speaker: sneak
text: Crack the stones with your hammer!
say: Crack the stones with your hammer.
note: Phase two's instruction.

speaker: sneak
text: We have them all! Meet me at the Secret Cave.
say: We have them all. Meet me at the Secret Cave.
note: Where the quest parks until the cave, the ritual and the faeries are built. Same mid-line '!' fix.

speaker: seraphina
text: Axe!
note: The first of the barks: her naming what she just switched to or picked up. Every one of these is `seraphina_` followed by the game's own id for the thing, and src/voice/barks.ts derives the id rather than listing it — so a new tool is a line in this file and nothing else. The bang is line-final, which edge-tts does not pad; only a mid-line one costs a second of silence.

speaker: seraphina
text: Hammer!

speaker: seraphina
text: Malachite!

speaker: seraphina
text: Ruby!

speaker: seraphina
text: Sapphire!

speaker: seraphina
text: I need my axe!
note: Said at a tree with the hammer in her hand. It names the tool that would work, because the thing to learn is what to do — not that this did not.

speaker: seraphina
text: I need my hammer!
note: The same sentence from the other end: said at a gem rock with the axe out.

speaker: sneak
text: You made it! Stand by the fire.
say: You made it. Stand by the fire.
note: He is already in the cave when she gets there. Said on arrival, and what the yellow button replays until she is actually standing in the circle. Same mid-line '!' fix.

speaker: sneak
text: Press the red button!
note: The ritual, one instruction at a time. The colour word in the text is the reading material; the slot row shows the same colour as a dot, never a letter. Bangs here are line-final and cost nothing.

speaker: sneak
text: Now the green button!

speaker: sneak
text: Now the blue button!

speaker: sneak
text: Try the red one!
note: A wrong press never goes backwards — it fizzles, everybody giggles, and he says which one it was again. See CLAUDE.md, 'No fail states'.

speaker: sneak
text: Try the green one!

speaker: sneak
text: Try the blue one!

speaker: sneak
text: Faeries! Real faeries!
note: The big moment. Mid-line bang split, so the second half does not start a second late.

speaker: hazel
text: So pretty!
note: Hazel came to the cave too, and this is the whole of what she has to say about faeries.

speaker: sneak
text: We did it! Thank you, Seraphina.
say: We did it, thank you Seraphina.
note: Shown with a bang and spoken with a comma. The first attempt at this only swapped the '!' for a '.', which buys the same ~0.9 s of dead air — a full stop is not the fix, a comma is. The second comma goes too: 'thank you, Seraphina' would be a third pause in a five-word line. See engineering.md, 'Voice'.

speaker: sneak
text: And this shiny gold coin is for you!
note: The last line of the quest, and the first coin in the game. His, out of his own mouth — he is handing her something. One sentence with no punctuation in the middle of it, so edge-tts has nowhere to put a second of silence, and the trailing '!' is free. 'Gold coin' is the pair of words the whole line exists to teach: it is said as the coin flies across the screen into the row, so the words and the picture are one event. See RoomScene.payUp.

speaker: hazel
text: Three little bunnies are stuck in the woods!
note: The bunny rescue, offered. One sentence with nothing in the middle of it, so edge-tts has nowhere to put a second of silence and the trailing bang is free. 'Bunnies' is in every line of this quest — she cannot read the word yet and hearing it nine times in an afternoon is how that changes.

speaker: hazel
text: Little trees are all around the bunnies! Go and find them.
say: Little trees are all around the bunnies, go and find them.
note: The second half of the offer, and phase one's instruction — the same line doing both, the way sneak_quest_stones does. Comma where the text has a bang: a mid-line '!' buys ~0.9 s of a lit sentence with no word lit.

speaker: hazel
text: Chop the little trees to free the bunnies!
note: Phase two. The verb and the reason in one breath, because what she has to hold in her head is why she is swinging.

speaker: hazel
text: Bunnies love carrots! Find three in the woods.
say: Bunnies love carrots, find three in the woods.
note: Phase three. Same mid-line '!' fix.

speaker: hazel
text: Give a bunny a carrot and walk it home to me!
note: Phase four, and the whole mechanic in one sentence: a carrot, a bunny, a walk. 'One at a time' is deliberately not in it — being told a rule she has not broken yet is a rule she will not remember, and the game says so out loud the moment she tries. See seraphina_one_bunny.

speaker: hazel
text: Two more bunnies to go!
note: Said at the den as the first one arrives. Pre-cut with the number in it, because there is no synthesiser in this game and there is never going to be one — two counts means two clips and a lookup. See BUNNIES_LEFT in RoomScene.

speaker: hazel
text: One more bunny to go!
note: And the second. There is no third: the third one home is not a count, it is the end of the quest.

speaker: hazel
text: All three bunnies are home!
note: The big moment of the second quest, said over the celebration at the den.

speaker: hazel
text: The bunnies want you to have this shiny gold coin!
note: The gift line, and hers rather than Seraphina's — she is standing at the den handing something over, which is somebody talking and not the world's own voice, exactly like sneak_coin. 'Gold coin' is the pair of words the line exists to teach and it is said as the coin flies across the screen. One sentence with no punctuation in the middle of it.

speaker: seraphina
text: Bunny!
note: A naming bark, derived from the id the way every other one is — see src/voice/barks.ts. Said as a bunny takes the carrot and falls in behind her. The bang is line-final, which costs nothing.

speaker: seraphina
text: Carrot!
note: The same, as one comes off the ground. One word for all three carrots: 'carrot_1' is not a thing anybody says out loud, and the noun is what is being taught.

speaker: seraphina
text: One bunny at a time, silly!
note: Tagging a second bunny while one is already following. The wrong answer is a funny nothing and never a buzzer — nothing is taken, no carrot is spent, and the bunny she already has carries on walking behind her. 'Silly' is aimed at herself, which is the only direction this game ever aims it. See CLAUDE.md, 'No fail states'.

speaker: seraphina
text: The bunny wants a carrot!
note: Pressing green at a bunny with an empty pocket. It names the fix rather than the failure, exactly like seraphina_need_axe: what she needs is the thing to go and do.

speaker: hazel
text: Will you read me a story?
note: Storytime, offered — the third quest, and Hazel's second. One sentence with nothing in the middle of it, so edge-tts has nowhere to put a second of silence. 'Story' and 'read' are the two words this whole quest exists to teach and they are both in the first thing anybody says about it.

speaker: hazel
text: There is a storybook on the bookshelf!
note: The second half of the offer and phase one's instruction — one line doing both, the way sneak_quest_stones and hazel_quest_pen do. The trailing bang is free; a mid-line one would cost ~0.9 s of a lit sentence with no word lit.

speaker: hazel
text: Come and sit on the rug with me!
note: Phase two: the walk across the living room. 'The rug' rather than a direction, because the rug is the thing that is glowing and she can see it from the bookshelf.

speaker: hazel
text: Press the green button to open the book!
note: Phase three, and what the yellow button replays until the book is open. It names the colour and never the letter, the same way the ritual's lines do — the dot on the pad under her thumb is the same green.

speaker: hazel
text: All the way to the moon!
note: What she says as the first page turns. The reaction belongs to the page just finished rather than the one arriving, so it is a thing said about a story and not a caption on one. It is spoken in the gap between the leaf going over and the new page starting to read itself — see RoomScene.turnPage.

speaker: hazel
text: A baby dragon!
note: The second page. Short on purpose: three delighted noises and one big line at the end is the shape, and a paragraph between pages would be the grown-up talking over the story.

speaker: hazel
text: Sparkles everywhere!
note: The third page.

speaker: hazel
text: That was the best story ever! Thank you Seraphina.
say: That was the best story ever, thank you Seraphina.
note: The last page, and the bigger line the whole read has been building to — nothing follows it but the book closing. Comma where the text has a bang: the mid-line '!' silence again.

speaker: hazel
text: Big hug! I love story time.
say: Big hug, I love story time.
note: The celebration beat, said while she leans over and bumps into her — there is no hug animation in the pack and there is not going to be one, so the hug is the movement and this is the word for it. Mid-line '!' split.

speaker: hazel
text: Here is a shiny gold coin for the best reader!
note: The gift line, hers rather than Seraphina's — she is handing something over, exactly like sneak_coin and hazel_bunny_coin. 'Gold coin' is the pair of words it exists to teach and it is said as the coin flies across the screen. One sentence with no punctuation in the middle of it.

speaker: seraphina
text: Storybook!
note: A naming bark, said as she takes it off the shelf. Not `seraphina_book`: that one is already the bookshelf's own line, 'I want to read a book!'. The compound word is what she is being taught anyway, and every other bark in the game is the noun for the thing in her hands. See src/voice/barks.ts.

speaker: seraphina
text: Pip the dog zoomed up to the moon!
note: Book #1, page one. The four book pages are the only lines in the game with a prosody override on them: `rate` here replaces the seraphina speaker's -8% outright rather than compounding with it, so -22% is fourteen points slower than everything else she says — a deliberate storybook pace, read to somebody rather than said to them. It is also the slowest thing in the game bar seraphina_sparky, which is a phonics line and not a sentence.

speaker: seraphina
text: On the moon Pip met a baby dragon!

speaker: seraphina
text: The dragon sneezed sparkles all over Pip!

speaker: seraphina
text: Now Pip and the dragon are best friends!

speaker: seraphina
text: I read my friend a whole story.
note: A day the story was read cover to cover. 'My friend' rather than her name, for seraphina_recap_errand's reason: nobody in the game has ever said it out loud, and bedtime is not where a name should be introduced. Third in the recap's order — under the two bigger finished jobs and over the errand. See src/state/recap.ts.

speaker: seraphina
text: I took three little bunnies home to their den.
note: A day the bunny rescue was finished. It sits beside the faerie line in the recap's order because they are the two ways an afternoon can have finished something, and no day can be both. See src/state/recap.ts.

speaker: seraphina
text: We called real faeries out of the fire.
note: The bedtime recap: what she says lying in the dark with the stars up, chosen by what the day's store says actually happened. See src/state/recap.ts, which owns the order they are picked in. All of these are hers and first person — she is remembering her own day, so the narrative-voice rule is not even a question here. None of them has a mid-line '!', which is the one thing that costs a second of silence with no word lit.

speaker: seraphina
text: I helped my friend look for magic stones.
note: A day she took the job and did not finish it. 'My friend' rather than his name: nobody in the game has ever said it out loud, and bedtime is not where a name should be introduced.

speaker: seraphina
text: I cracked a magic stone right open.
note: A day with a hammer in it.

speaker: seraphina
text: I chopped a whole tree down with my axe.
note: A day in the wood. Last in the order, because felling one is a thing she can do all afternoon.

speaker: seraphina
text: Goodnight, world. See you in the morning.
say: Goodnight world, see you in the morning.
note: Always the last thing said, every night, whatever else happened. A day with nothing in it is only this line — which is why it has to work alone, and why it says goodnight to the world rather than to whatever she just did. Spoken with the full stop moved to a comma: edge-tts leaves nearly a second of silence after a mid-line '.', which measured at 0.94s here — a second of a lit-up sentence with no word lit, at the one moment she is meant to be watching it. Same fix the mid-line '!' lines use.
